status_summary: Executive Order 14169 (signed 2025-01-20) paused new obligations and disbursements of foreign development assistance for a 90-day review under guidelines set by the Secretary of State, with a Secretary of State waiver power, and a State Department cable of 2025-01-24, reported by AP, extended the pause to nearly all foreign assistance, with exceptions for emergency food aid and military aid to Israel and Egypt. State and USAID began sending stop-work orders to implementing partners on 2025-01-24 and State issued a waiver for life-saving humanitarian aid on 2025-01-28, according to Human Rights Watch. A presidential memorandum of 2025-01-20 froze federal civilian hiring government-wide, with exceptions including political appointments, and a 2025-07-07 memorandum extended it to 2025-10-15; no separate State freeze on Foreign Service recruiting was found, though Government Executive reported in March 2026 that State brought on nearly 100 new Foreign Service officers in 2025 while onboarding of Pickering and Rangel fellows was delayed. On 2025-03-10 the Secretary of State announced that the program review, which AP says was carried out by political appointees at State and DOGE teams, was ending, with about 5,200 of 6,200 USAID programs eliminated. EO 14222 (2025-02-26) separately required agencies to review existing contracts and grants, prioritizing funds to foreign entities, and to record a justification for each payment, a government-wide step parallel to the Mandate's call to freeze contracts and payments. Courts limited the payment freeze: after the Supreme Court on 2025-03-05 declined to vacate a district court order on payment for completed work, the district court on 2025-03-10 enjoined giving effect to pause-related actions taken from 2025-01-20 to 2025-02-13; the D.C. Circuit later vacated the injunction's impoundment portion, and the case remains open. The aid-restructuring results are covered in c09-01 and c09-02, and treaty review in c06-08.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14169 paused new obligations and disbursements of foreign development assistance for 90 days pending program reviews under State guidelines, with a Secretary of State waiver power.

A presidential memorandum froze hiring of federal civilian employees government-wide, with exceptions including national security, public safety and political appointments; it does not mention the State Department or the Foreign Service.
State Department and USAID officials began sending stop-work orders to thousands of implementing partners, according to Human Rights Watch.

A State Department cable to embassies, reported by AP, barred new spending on nearly all foreign assistance, with exceptions for emergency food aid and military aid to Israel and Egypt, and set review standards within about a month and a review within three months to inform the Secretary's recommendations.
State issued a waiver allowing certain life-saving humanitarian assistance to continue, with guidance on 2025-02-06 extending it to HIV treatment and related costs.

EO 14222 directs agency heads to record a written justification for each payment under covered contracts and grants and to review existing contracts and grants within 30 days, prioritizing funds to educational institutions and foreign entities, and to terminate or modify them where appropriate; a government-wide step parallel to the Mandate's call to freeze contracts and payments.
The Supreme Court denied the government's application to vacate a district court order requiring payment for completed work, with four justices dissenting (AIDS Vaccine Advocacy Coalition case).
timeline.source: Supreme Court of the United States

timeline.event: The Secretary of State announced the review of USAID programs was ending, with about 5,200 of 6,200 programs eliminated and the rest to be run by State; AP reported that political appointees at State and DOGE teams carried out the review.

The district court issued a preliminary injunction against giving effect to the State guidance and pause-related actions taken from 2025-01-20 to 2025-02-13, including payment for work completed before 2025-02-13, and against unlawful impoundment of foreign aid (per the Civil Rights Litigation Clearinghouse).
A new presidential memorandum extended the federal hiring freeze to 2025-10-15.

The D.C. Circuit vacated the impoundment portion of the preliminary injunction, holding the plaintiffs lacked an APA cause of action under the Impoundment Control Act; an amended judgment issued the mandate on 2025-08-28 (per the Clearinghouse). The case remains open.

Government Executive reported that State brought on nearly 100 new Foreign Service officers in 2025, that more than 50 Pickering and Rangel fellows were still awaiting onboarding, and that the 2026 fellowship application cycles were on hold.

title: Freeze foreign aid, payments and hiring at inauguration pending a political review
uncertainties: The January 2025 State cable was not read; its scope rests on AP's 2025-01-24 report, and the stop-work and waiver dates rest on Human Rights Watch. The 2025-03-10 date of the review announcement is taken from same-day AP syndications; the ABC copy cited gives only a weekday. Court events after 2025-03-05 rest on the Civil Rights Litigation Clearinghouse summary (last author entry 2025-11-23, docket updated 2026-02-21), not on the orders; whether the non-impoundment portion of the 2025-03-10 injunction is still in force was not confirmed. No State-specific freeze on contracts beyond foreign aid, or on Foreign Service recruiting, was found. Partial overlap with c09-01 (the same 90-day pause as the first step of the USAID restructuring) and c09-02 (aid cuts) is a cross-reference, not a duplicate: this record tracks the Mandate's separate chapter 6 call (page 174) for an across-the-board freeze at inauguration, including hiring and contracts, pending political review. The c06-08 record on treaty review was not opened in this review.
